slides.title: What Zillow Home Loans does
slides.lead: Zillow Home Loans is Zillow’s affiliated mortgage lender.
slides.body:
For the buyer

A loan officer reviews financing options, explains the payment and cash needed, and guides the loan process. ZHL offers purchase and refinance loans.

For the agent

You coordinate property questions, financing progress and transaction deadlines with the loan officer. The loan officer determines loan eligibility and approval.

For this training

Learn what ZHL provides so you can explain the reason for an introduction. The buyer decides which lender to use.

Zillow Home Loans overview ↗ · Reviewed September 17, 2026

slides.title: Know the loan options you can ask ZHL about
slides.lead: Name the option, then let the loan officer explain whether it fits this buyer.
slides.body:
Conventional

A mortgage without a federal government guarantee. Ask about available fixed-rate and adjustable-rate options.

FHA

Insured by the Federal Housing Administration. Ask about down payment and mortgage insurance when comparing it with a conventional loan.

VA

For eligible veterans, service members and certain surviving spouses. The loan officer confirms eligibility and explains any funding fee.

Jumbo

A loan above the applicable conforming limit. Ask which limit applies to the property and what ZHL requires for the larger amount.

ZHL also offers refinance options. Rates, down payments and program requirements must be confirmed for the individual file. ZHL currently lists availability in U.S. states except New York; territories are excluded.

slides.title: Understand the stages before calling a buyer approved
slides.lead: Ask what the lender has reviewed and what still needs to happen.
slides.body:
01

Pre-qualification

An initial estimate using self-reported income and assets plus a soft credit check. It does not mean the documents have all been verified.

02

Verified pre-approval

The buyer submits documents to confirm financial information. Ask what has been verified and which conditions remain.

03

Final approval and funding

The lender must complete the remaining borrower and property requirements. A pre-approval letter does not guarantee funding.

ZHL pre-qualification and pre-approval FAQ ↗ · Reviewed September 17, 2026

slides.title: Explain the credit check without making a promise
slides.lead: Use this wording when a buyer asks whether checking financing affects their credit.
slides.body:
“ZHL’s pre-qualification starts with a soft credit check. Before you go further, let’s have the loan officer explain which credit checks your application will need.”

What agents should know

A hard inquiry may be required later. Do not say that the entire loan process has no effect on credit.

What the buyer should confirm

Ask the loan officer to explain the credit inquiry before proceeding with the next step.

slides.title: Decide whether a lender introduction fits the timing
slides.lead: TRU’s introduction guidance: confirm the buyer’s plans before transferring the lead.
slides.body:
01

Buying within six months

If the buyer wants to purchase, has a financing question and wants help, offer an introduction. A short timeline alone is not permission to transfer.

02

More than six months away

Usually continue agent follow-up rather than transfer now. At twelve months out, ask what sets the timing, save the reason and agree when to revisit financing.

03

Already supported or not interested

If they have a lender and do not want another conversation, respect that. Confirm what is already in progress and continue working with their chosen lender.

This is TRU’s timing guidance, not a ZHL lending requirement. If a buyer asks for financing advice earlier, clarify the question and offer a conversation when it would help.

slides.title: Ask about the buyer’s plan when they raise a credit concern
slides.lead: Do not automatically transfer someone because they mention a credit problem.
slides.body:
No near-term purchase or request for help

Ask when they expect to buy and whether they want help now. If they are not ready to act, agree on a follow-up date instead of sending an unexpected lender referral.

Wants to buy soon and asks about options

For “I want to buy in three months and need to know what is possible,” offer a loan-officer conversation about eligibility and steps. Confirm that they want the introduction.

“Are you looking for help understanding your options now, or would you rather revisit this closer to when you’re ready?”

Let the loan officer assess credit and loan eligibility. Do not promise approval, a workaround or a credit-repair timeline.

slides.title: Offer the introduction at the end of the appointment
slides.lead: First ask: “Have you already spoken with a lender about your budget?”
slides.body:
If they need a lender
“Since you’re hoping to buy in the next three months, it would help to know what payment you’re comfortable with and what you can qualify for. I work with a loan officer at Zillow Home Loans. Would you like me to introduce you?”
If they say yes
“Would you prefer a group text or email? What time would be good for a call?”

Use their answer in the introduction. Ask the loan officer to confirm the time before telling the buyer it is scheduled.

If they decline: “No problem. How would you like to handle financing from here?” The buyer chooses the lender.

slides.title: Connect the buyer and loan officer in Follow Up Boss
slides.lead: After the buyer agrees, make the connection in their contact record.
slides.body:
01

Select the loan officer

Open the contact’s Financing section and select the lender field. Choose an available ZHL loan officer or Transfer to your ZHL team.

02

Add the agreed context

Include the purchase timing, question they want answered, and preferred contact time. Confirm the assignment, then send the group introduction.

03

Check the connection

Confirm receipt and the call time with both people. Assignment alone does not confirm that they have spoken.

The feature requires Zillow two-way integration and your Zillow profile linked to FUB. If the option is missing, ask your administrator to check those connections.

slides.title: Send an introduction that explains why they are connecting
slides.lead: Sample wording for the practice case. Replace the names, goal and time with what the buyer agreed to.
slides.body:
Group text or email

Jordan, meet Casey, a loan officer with Zillow Home Loans.

Casey, Jordan is hoping to buy in the next three months and wants to understand the monthly payment and cash needed. Jordan asked me to connect you.

Jordan is free tomorrow at three. Casey, does that work for a call?

After sending

Confirm that Casey received the introduction and replied about the time. Tell Jordan when the call is confirmed.

If there is no reply

Contact the loan officer directly. Update the buyer at the time you promised and agree on another time if needed.

Save the follow-up

Record the buyer’s permission, the introduction and the call status in FUB. Create a task to check whether the call happened.

slides.title: Practice the introduction in breakout rooms
slides.lead: Groups of three. Start at the end of the first appointment; the buyer wants to purchase within three months.
slides.body:
Set up · 1 minute

Assign agent, buyer and loan officer/observer. Use the Jordan practice card. The observer also responds as the loan officer during the handoff.

Three rounds · 4 minutes each

Agent: ask about financing, offer the introduction and arrange the connection (2 minutes). Observer: give one specific correction (1 minute). Agent: repeat that part (1 minute). Rotate so everyone practices as the agent.

What to listen for

Did the agent check timing and the existing lender, explain the reason for ZHL, ask permission, and confirm who will contact whom and when?

Practice only. Do not send a real referral, enter real buyer details or submit a loan application during the exercise. Use the Jordan buyer card below; use the other cards when repeating the practice.

cases.name: Jordan · first appointment, buying within three months
cases.quote: I definitely want to keep looking and buy a home. I have not spoken with a lender yet. I want to understand the monthly payment and cash I will need.
cases.goal: Buyer: accept an introduction if the agent explains the reason and asks. Prefer a group text and offer tomorrow at three. Loan officer/observer: confirm that time only when asked. Give one correction and let the agent retry.

cases.name: Morgan · twelve months away
cases.quote: I am only looking ahead. My job move is about a year away, and I do not need financing help right now.
cases.goal: Agent: ask what sets the timing, respect that no lender help is wanted now, and agree when to revisit. Do not transfer simply to complete a referral.

cases.name: Alex · credit concern and a three-month goal
cases.quote: I want to buy in the next three months, but I have a credit issue and need to understand whether I have any options.
cases.goal: Agent: ask whether Alex wants a loan officer to review the options. Explain the purpose and get permission; do not promise approval or decide credit eligibility yourself.

cases.name: Taylor · already has a lender
cases.quote: I already have a lender I trust, and I do not want another introduction.
cases.goal: Agent: respect the decision. Ask what has already been completed and agree how you will coordinate with the chosen lender.
